channel.title: Rousan
channel.description: Personal Website of Kazi Abu Rousan

item.title: Tree Codes 5: The Code
item.description: Part 5 of recreating Hernquist (1987): the complete Julia source for the Barnes-Hut tree code, the test suite, and how to run everything yourself.

item.title: The Expanding Universe I — Geometry
item.description: Part 1 of The Expanding Universe. Deriving the Robertson–Walker metric from scratch — the embedding of the symmetric three-spaces, the reduction to a(t) and k, the S_k(χ) curvature function and conformal time — with the expansion history, horizon and curvature radius computed in Cosmic.jl.

item.title: The Expanding Universe II — Kinematics
item.description: Part 2 of The Expanding Universe. Deriving the geodesic equation, the E ∝ 1/a redshift, the Hubble–Lemaître law, and the luminosity and angular-diameter distances from first principles — with distances for flat, open and closed universes all computed in Cosmic.jl.

item.title: The Expanding Universe with Cosmic.jl
item.description: A five-part tour through cosmology (Baumann, Chapters 2, 5 and 6): the homogeneous universe's geometry, kinematics, dynamics and thermal history, then how tiny perturbations grow into galaxies — with every result checked numerically against my Julia package Cosmic.jl.

item.title: The Expanding Universe V — Perturbations
item.description: Part 5 of The Expanding Universe. Deriving the growth of structure — the Newtonian fluid equations, the relativistic generalisation in the conformal Newtonian gauge, gauge freedom, and the Mészáros effect — with the growth factor, the perturbation hierarchy and the matter power spectrum all computed in Cosmic.jl.

item.title: The Expanding Universe IV — Our Universe
item.description: Part 4 of The Expanding Universe. The measured cosmic budget, the age, matter–radiation equality, and the thermal history — deriving the photon density and the Saha recombination equation, with the ionization history, last scattering and the BAO sound horizon computed in Cosmic.jl against Baumann's Table 2.1.

item.title: The Expanding Universe III — Dynamics
item.description: Part 3 of The Expanding Universe. Deriving the continuity equation, the Friedmann equations and the exact radiation/matter/Λ solutions — with the density eras, the expansion history, and the fate of flat, open and closed universes all computed in Cosmic.jl.

item.title: Minkowski Functionals: Measuring the Shape of the Universe
item.description: A first-principles guide to Minkowski functionals: from 'what is shape?' through Hadwiger's theorem, curvature, the Steiner inflation formula, and the Hermite-ladder Gaussian predictions, to measuring non-Gaussianity in cosmology. Physical analogies (a flooding landscape), full derivations, symbolic checks in SymPy and WolframScript, numerical checks in Python and Julia, and an interactive 3D water-level widget.

item.title: Grassmann Algebra: Multiplying with Area and Orientation
item.description: A friendly, visual introduction to Grassmann (exterior) algebra: the wedge product, bivectors, orientation, multivector grades, and the tensor-algebra quotient definition — with runnable SageMath and SymPy code. The first part of a mini-series leading to Clifford algebras and spinors.

item.title: Legendre's Tranformation: A intuitive approach
item.description: A brief discussion on Legendre Transformation

item.title: Special Function and it's generation
item.description: A brief discussion on Introduction on how to generate special functions using the tools of linear algebra.

item.title: Introduction to Monte Carlo Integration
item.description: A brief discussion on Introduction to Monte Carlo Integration. Here we will see how to perform this in julia language and also it's theory.

item.title: Fast and Curious
item.description: A blog on comparing speed of different languages.

item.title: Playing with Tupper's Formula in Julia
item.description: A brief intro to Tupper's Formula with Julia. Here we will see how to perform this in julia language.

item.title: Introduction to Monte Carlo Integration
item.description: A brief discussion on Introduction to Monte Carlo Integration. Here we will see how to perform this in julia language and also it's theory.

item.title: Reciprocals of Primes
item.description: A brief discussion on the fact that taking the reciprocals of primes will generate numbers which repeat after certain digits. Here we will understand why this happens and will write a code to find out the period.

item.title: About / CV
item.description: Kazi Abu Rousan — PhD student in Cosmology at NISER. Research in early-universe cosmology, recombination and CMB spectral distortions, with scientific computing in Julia and Python.
